title: Release briefing: pocket-map & skipwave rollout schedule (Jul 2027)
content:
Context and high-level intent:
This doc is a compact preflight + runbook + small release-notes draft for the skipwave rollout of the response-routing optimization (v3.8.0) — goal is to validate latency tail improvements in production without increasing error-rate or cost. Use as the pocket-map for operators during the 72h watch window.

Quick TL;DR:
- Release: inference-runtime v3.8.0 (routing opt)
- Window: Jul 12 2027 02:00 UTC -> Jul 15 2027 02:00 UTC (72h watch)
- Primary metric focus: p95 latency, server-side error-rate (5xx), end-to-end tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens
- Rollout method: skipwave canary (non-linear waves to reduce coupling with autoscale)
- Rollout owner (day shift): Miguel Alvarez; night shift: Rae Kim; backup oncall: Tomoko Sato

Preflight (must complete before any traffic shift):
- [ ] All unit/integration tests green on main branch (PR #1203)
- [ ] Staging soak: 24h at median load (match prod p50 token distribution) — staging run id: stg-2027-07-07-09
- [ ] Canary image pushed and verified in registry (sha: sha256:9b3f7c)
- [ ] TF/Config migration tested (feature flag schema backwards compatible)
- [ ] Load-tests: 2x normal sustained for 30m with no unexplained 5xx
- [ ] Observability: dashboards live for p50/p95/p99, token throughput, cost-per-token, cold-starts, cache-hit-rate
- [ ] Alerting: temporary canary paging thresholds set (see telemetry thresholds below)
- [ ] Rollback artifact prepared and smoke-tested (v3.7.4 stable)
- [ ] Oncall rota published and Slack bridge created (#release-skipwave-jul12)

Skipwave rollout schedule (compact):
- Wave 0 (sanity): 0 -> 0.5% traffic, duration 10m. Verify health endpoints + smoke suite.
- Wave 1: 0.5% -> 5% over 30m (skip some intermediate waves if stable)
- Wave 2: 5% -> 20% over 50m
- Wave 3: 20% -> 40% over 60m
- Wave 4: 40% -> 70% over 90m
- Wave 5: 70% -> 100% over 2h (final ramp may be extended if SLOs waver)
Notes: skipwave means we intentionally skip narrow midpoints between large jumps (e.g., 5%->20% instead of 5->10->15->20) to expose autoscale and routing interactions early. Keep strong telemetry sampling during jumps.

Telemetry thresholds (temporary canary alerting):
- p95 latency: alert if increase > 20% relative to baseline (baseline = last 7d median during peak hours)
- 5xx rate: alert if > 0.5% absolute or > 2x baseline
- tail error spikes: page for any sustained 3m window with >0.25% errors and >10 requests/s
- cold-starts: alert if cold-start rate increases by >10% absolute
- cost-per-1k-tokens: notify if +15% sustained over 30m
Escalation: primary oncall -> backup -> engineering lead (Jared Bloom) -> SRE manager.

Canary smoke checklist (run after each wave stabilizes):
- [ ] Smoke: health-checks OK on all nodes in canary pool
- [ ] Run sample prompts across a fixed eval set (prompt-set id: eval-routing-120) and compare deltas to baseline (fuzzy-match < 3% change in correctness scores)
- [ ] Check KV cache-hit-rate (should not drop > 5% from baseline)
- [ ] Verify routing fallback behavior: simulate busy region failover
- [ ] Confirm no increase in model divergence for streaming responses (manual spot-checks)
- [ ] Confirm A/B logging is capturing both paths with correct metadata keys

Traffic shaping and capacity notes:
- Autoscale policy: min 10 GPU nodes, target CPU utilization 65%, max burst = +30% capacity for 20m windows
- During ramp windows, keep burst capacity available; if autoscaler fails to provision within 3m during a ramp, pause rollout and roll back last wave.
- Rate-limiter thresholds should remain unchanged; if we hit user-facing throttles during ramp, pause and investigate.

Rollback decision matrix (fast rollback recommended upon trigger):
Triggers that require immediate rollback:
- p95 latency spikes > 40% and user-facing errors increase within 15m
- 5xx rate > 1% sustained 5m and not explained by release-adjacent infra change
- Significant drop (>20%) in throughput for stable budgets
Rollback steps (fast path):
1) Announce on #release-skipwave-jul12 "ROLLBACK: reason" and tag oncall
2) Shift weighted routing back to previous deployment (v3.7.4) using traffic router (playbook command: router shift revert --tag v3.7.4)
3) Monitor key signals for 10m, then widen observation window to 30m
4) Open incident if rollback does not restore baseline within 30m

Operator commands & handy snippets:
- Verify canary pool health: /infra/canary-health --pool skipwave-2027-07
- Trigger immediate rollback: /router set-weight --service inference-api --to-tag v3.7.4 --percent 100
- Capture heap/profile from node: ssh operator@canary-node-XX 'curl localhost:1234/pprof > /tmp/pprof-$(date +%s).pb'

Night/weekend specific notes:
- If ramp crosses into night shift, reduce step-size (no more than 15% jumps) and extend stabilization windows to 45m.
- Keep one senior SRE reachable during night 00:00-08:00 UTC.

Post-release retro template (to fill after watch window):
- What went well?
- What surprised us?
- Incidents/near-misses and root cause notes
- Telemetry gaps we noticed / dashboards to add
- Process tweaks (e.g., change skipwave cadence or ramp policy)

Release notes (draft) — v3.8.0
Highlights:
- Response routing optimization: smarter shard-aware routing to reduce token latency for long-context sessions (p95 gains in internal tests ~12–18% depending on workload)
- Safety: additional checks on request routing to prevent hot-shard thrash; new flags to opt-in/out per-tenant
- Observability: new tracing fields (route_id, shard_score) exposed in request logs and APM spans

Behavioral changes / compatibility:
- Default routing now prefers shard-local pools; if you relied on global round-robin to spread costs, expect short-lived traffic concentration during initial rollout. If this impacts you, contact support to opt-out of shard-local preference.
- Feature flags: routing.opt_in_shard_local (boolean, default=true), routing.sample_trace (boolean, default=false)

Migration steps for platform teams:
1) If you manage custom rate-limits, verify they are per-route aware (see docs/concepts/routing-fields)
2) If you have infra that assumes global uniform request distribution (rare), validate against staging with option routing.opt_in_shard_local=false
3) Update SLO dashboards to include new tracing tag route_id

Known issues (to call out proactively):
- Intermittent high tail latency for a specific 3rd-party model adapter (adapter-adx-2) under high concurrency — mitigation: adapter-level backpressure currently in testing, we may toggle adapter-adx-2 off for some tenants during rollouts if noisy.
- Tracing samples not visible in some older telemetry exports; exported spans will be retried in the next pipeline run — not user-facing but annoying for debugging.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Confirm with infra whether node-termination drain window (currently 120s) needs extension for this release — @Tomoko to confirm before wave 2.
- Should we pre-seed KV cache in canary nodes with customer prefixes for the largest tenants? Pros/cons in staging vs. warmup observational noise.
- Consider adding a short-lived dashboard to show per-tenant routing concentration (helpful for customers running quota alarms).

Appendix: quick contact list
- Release owner (day): Miguel Alvarez (miguel@redwood.ai)
- Release owner (night): Rae Kim (rae@redwood.ai)
- SRE lead: Tomoko Sato (tomoko@redwood.ai)
- Engineering lead: Jared Bloom (jared@redwood.ai)

End of pocket-map — keep this file as the single source during run. Update with timestamps and final retro notes after watch window.
